title: Calcaratarin D exerts neuroprotective effects in Alzheimer's disease mouse model by inhibiting CERT-mediated NF-kappaB pathway.
authors: Pan, Jin-Zhi; Yu, Meng-Yao; Tian, Ming-Zhu; Liu, Run; Zhao, Wei; Luo, Qian
one_liner_zh: 该文研究天然化合物CalD在阿尔茨海默病模型中的神经保护作用，涉及NF-kappaB通路和分子对接，但核心是疾病机制与药物效应，非蛋白质-DNA互作或TF-DNA结合建模，与本课题无关。
abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is a neurodegenerative disease characterized by beta-amyloid plaque accumulation, neuroinflammation, and dysregulation of sphingolipid metabolism, mainly manifested as irreversible cognitive decline and memory loss. A key pathological hallmark of AD is neuroinflammation, largely fueled by the persistent stimulation of microglia and subsequent pro-inflammatory cytokine production, which worsens disease development. Calcaratarin D (CalD), a ladanane-type diterpenoid sourced from Hedychium flavum rhizomes, has been reported to exhibit significant anti-inflammatory effects. However, its potential therapeutic benefits in AD remain unknown. Therefore, this research focused on exploring the neuroprotective effects of CalD in AD and elucidating its potential mechanisms. We established a mouse model of AD by targeting delivery of Abeta(1)(-)(4)(2) oligomers to the hippocampus. Behavioral tests showed that CalD significantly improved the memory loss and spatial learning ability of AD mice. Western blotting and immunofluorescence staining further confirmed that CalD effectively reduced Abeta deposition and inhibited the excessive activation of microglia. Network pharmacology analysis found that the mechanism of action of CalD mainly involved inflammatory signaling pathways and sphingolipid metabolism. Subsequently, in vivo and in vitro experiments confirmed that CalD could inhibit the excessive activation of the TLR4/NF-kappaB/NLRP3 signaling pathway and restore the ceramide homeostasis in AD mice. On this basis, molecular docking and small interfering RNA experiments further clarified that CalD played an anti-inflammatory by targeting CERT. In summary, these findings indicate that CalD exerts neuroprotective effects by modulating neuroinflammation and ceramide metabolic dysregulation, suggesting that CalD has therapeutic potential in AD.
abstract_zh: 阿尔茨海默病（Alzheimer's disease, AD）是一种神经退行性疾病，其特征为β-淀粉样蛋白斑块积累、神经炎症以及鞘脂代谢失调，主要表现为不可逆的认知衰退和记忆丧失。AD的一个关键病理标志是神经炎症，主要由小胶质细胞的持续刺激及随后的促炎细胞因子产生所驱动，这加剧了疾病的发展。Calcaratarin D（CalD）是一种源自黄花姜（Hedychium flavum）根茎的拉丹烷型二萜类化合物，据报道具有显著的抗炎作用。然而，其在AD中的潜在治疗益处尚不清楚。因此，本研究旨在探讨CalD在AD中的神经保护作用，并阐明其潜在机制。我们通过靶向递送Aβ(1-42)寡聚体至海马体建立了AD小鼠模型。行为学测试显示，CalD显著改善了AD小鼠的记忆丧失和空间学习能力。Western blotting和免疫荧光染色进一步证实，CalD有效减少了Aβ沉积，并抑制了小胶质细胞的过度激活。网络药理学分析发现，CalD的作用机制主要涉及炎症信号通路和鞘脂代谢。随后，体内和体外实验证实，CalD能够抑制TLR4/NF-κB/NLRP3信号通路的过度激活，并恢复AD小鼠中的神经酰胺稳态。在此基础上，分子对接和小干扰RNA实验进一步阐明，CalD通过靶向CERT发挥抗炎作用。总之，这些发现表明，CalD通过调节神经炎症和神经酰胺代谢失调发挥神经保护作用，提示CalD在AD中具有治疗潜力。
